blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interprofessional coordination for guideline-based diagnostic evaluation of suspected idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
stem: A nurse helps coordinate the evaluation of a client with newly detected interstitial lung disease who is clinically suspected of having idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Which action best aligns with the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT diagnostic approach?

options.A: Facilitate multidisciplinary discussion that integrates the clinical findings and HRCT, with histopathology incorporated when it is available.
options.B: Use serum MMP-7 as the primary discriminator for IPF and arrange multidisciplinary review only when the biomarker result conflicts with imaging.
options.C: Have radiology establish the final diagnosis from HRCT alone and seek broader specialty review if the client later fails the initial treatment plan.
options.D: Begin disease-specific treatment from the clinical suspicion and postpone interdisciplinary diagnostic review until the response to therapy is known.

rationale: A is correct. The official 2018 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT diagnostic guideline conditionally suggests multidisciplinary discussion for diagnostic decision-making in patients with newly detected interstitial lung disease who are clinically suspected of having IPF. The current ATS implementation page continues to list that diagnostic guideline, and the current ATS clinical-practice-guideline index lists both the 2018 Diagnosis of IPF guideline and the 2022 IPF update. The 2022 update revised radiologic and histopathologic criteria and specific diagnostic questions and its diagnostic algorithm continues to use multidisciplinary discussion; for example, a probable-UIP HRCT pattern can support an IPF diagnosis after MDD in the appropriate clinical setting, and some indeterminate cases may be reclassified after MDD and/or additional consultation. B is incorrect because the 2018 guideline strongly recommends against measuring serum MMP-7, SPD, CCL-18, or KL-6 solely to distinguish IPF from other ILDs. C is incorrect because the guideline-based approach integrates clinical, radiologic, and when available pathologic information rather than assigning the final diagnosis to imaging alone. D is incorrect because multidisciplinary diagnostic review is part of diagnostic decision-making and should not be postponed merely to judge response to empiric disease-specific treatment.
educational_objective: Coordinate suspected-IPF evaluation through multidisciplinary integration of clinical, radiologic, and when available pathologic information rather than relying on an isolated biomarker, imaging opinion, or treatment trial.
source_organization: American Thoracic Society (ATS); European Respiratory Society (ERS); Japanese Respiratory Society (JRS); Asociación Latinoamericana de Tórax (ALAT); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: An Official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline; Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (an Update) and Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Adults; current ATS Clinical Practice Guidelines index; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: 2018 diagnostic guideline published 2018-09-01; 2022 update published 2022-05-01; both are still listed on the current ATS clinical-practice-guideline index rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: Current ATS Diagnosis of IPF implementation page lines 166-179 lists Raghu et al., AJRCCM 2018;198(5):e44-e68 and links the full guideline. Official 2018 guideline abstract/recommendations: for newly detected ILD clinically suspected of IPF, suggest multidisciplinary discussion for diagnostic decision-making; strongly recommend against serum MMP-7, SPD, CCL-18, or KL-6 solely to distinguish IPF from other ILDs. Current ATS CPG index lines 202-206 lists both the 2022 IPF update and the 2018 Diagnosis of IPF guideline. Official 2022 update, PubMed PMID 35486072 / Figure 10 text: probable-UIP cases can receive an IPF diagnosis after multidisciplinary discussion in the appropriate clinical setting; indeterminate cases may be reclassified after multidisciplinary discussion and/or additional consultation. The 2022 abstract states that the update revised radiological/histopathological criteria and addressed TBLC, genomic classifier testing, antacid medication, and antireflux surgery. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care supports multidisciplinary collaboration, referral coordination, and integration of information across the care team.
source_claim_supported: Fresh authoritative ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT evidence directly supports multidisciplinary diagnostic discussion for suspected IPF, rejects sole reliance on specified serum biomarkers to distinguish IPF from other ILDs, and shows that the 2022 update continues to incorporate MDD in the IPF diagnostic algorithm. Current ATS indexing confirms that both the 2018 diagnostic guideline and 2022 update remain active implementation resources.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess referral needs, coordinate care, communicate client information, and utilize resources to promote quality client care.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan evidence was visually verified earlier in this cleanup session. Q1924 currentness and clinical claims were verified using current ATS/Oxford/PubMed HTML; no new PDF evidence was analyzed for this resumed audit.
correction_summary: Q1924 was previously BLOCKED because ATS/current-source retrieval repeatedly failed. Fresh retrieval succeeded on 2026-08-20: the ATS implementation page is readable, the current ATS CPG index lists both the 2018 diagnostic guideline and 2022 update, the 2018 official publication directly supports MDD and the serum-biomarker recommendation, and the 2022 official PubMed record shows MDD remains in the diagnostic algorithm. The item was rebuilt to remove simplistic distractors and to test integration of clinical/HRCT/pathology information versus biomarker, imaging-only, or empiric-treatment shortcuts.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects guideline-supported multidisciplinary integration of clinical and HRCT information, with pathology incorporated when available.
option_audit.B: Plausible biomarker shortcut; incorrect because the guideline recommends against using specified serum biomarkers such as MMP-7 solely to distinguish IPF from other ILDs.
option_audit.C: Plausible imaging-centric shortcut; incorrect because IPF diagnosis is not assigned by radiology alone when multidisciplinary integration is indicated.
option_audit.D: Plausible empiric-treatment shortcut; incorrect because diagnostic MDD should not be deferred merely to assess response to disease-specific therapy.
